summary: The fixed 26-letter alphabet makes every source-faithful route-pricing method linear in the string length, while every aligned character can affect the answer and establishes a matching linear lower bound.

optimality.argument: In the worst case, changing either character at any unread aligned position changes the minimum transformation cost while preserving every source constraint. A correct algorithm must therefore inspect all n positions. The accepted implementation performs constant work per pair after fixed 26-entry preprocessing and matches this lower bound.

replacement_checks.evidence: An adversary can change an unread source or target character at any aligned position and thereby change its independent nonnegative contribution to the total.
Two 26-entry prefix arrays make both circular route costs constant-time queries, followed by one pass over the aligned string positions.
Authored cases cover identity, both wrap edges, departure-letter indexing, free long routes, every alphabet letter, mixed weights, maximum edge costs, and a total beyond 32-bit range.
